newsitem.title: USA: BNP shelves US debt issue after news leak.
newsitem.headline: BNP shelves US debt issue after news leak.

text.p: Banque Nationale de Paris on Thursday postponed its $350 million debt issue to avoid the impression of impropriety over the purchase of Credit Industriel Commercial, a syndicate official said.

The move came after an article in French newspaper Les Echos on Thursday reported that BNP appeared to be "better placed" than competitor Societe Generale in their bids to acquire state-owned Credit Industriel.

Offers from the two banks were both around six or seven billion francs, sources said, but the BNP proposal appeared technically superior, Les Echos said. Underwriters at lead manager Salomon Brothers received notice from BNP that the deal would be postponed until further notice, the syndicate official said. The 12-year issue was set to price on Thursday to yield 80 to 82 basis points over the U.S. Treasury curve.

"(BNP) can't confirm or deny anything; it is just concerned about press reports and they didn't want to give the impression that they knew something concerning any discussion with Treasury," said the official, who declined to be named.
The syndicate official called the postponement "prudent" given the uncertainties surrounding the situtation.

"Nobody knows what kind of a bid it is and nobody knows the terms of the bid," the official added. "They are not sure whether it will be viewed positively or negatively by the ratings agencies; there are just a lot of unknowns."

BNP is bound by a confidentiality agreement with the French government in connection with the bidding process, the official said. But because BNP is one of France's largest banks, he said it is no secret that it will look at Credit Industriele.
Neither BNP nor Societe General has confirmed it is making an offer for Credit Industriele.
